info.title: 1Platform API
info.description:
# 1Platform API

REST API powering the **1Platform** platform — content generation, SEO tooling, billing, invoicing, and third-party integrations.

---

## Authentication

1Platform uses a **two-token** authentication model:

| Token | Header | How to obtain | Purpose |
|-------|--------|---------------|---------|
| **App token** | `Authorization: Bearer <token>` | `POST /api/v1/auth/token` with your App API key | Identifies the calling application |
| **User token** | `x-user-token: <token>` | `POST /api/v1/users/token` with the user API key | Identifies the end user |

Most endpoints require **both** tokens. Exceptions are noted per endpoint.

## Quickstart

```bash
# 1. Get an app token
curl -X POST https://api.1platform.pro/api/v1/auth/token \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"apiKey": "ak-your-app-api-key"}'

# 2. Get a user token (requires app token)
curl -X POST https://api.1platform.pro/api/v1/users/token \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $APP_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"apiKey": "sk-user-api-key"}'

# 3. Call any protected endpoint (requires both tokens)
curl https://api.1platform.pro/api/v1/users/profile \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $APP_TOKEN" \
  -H "x-user-token: $USER_TOKEN"
```

## Base URL

All endpoints are prefixed with `/api/v1/`.

## Rate Limits

| Category | Limit |
|----------|-------|
| Health | 100 req/min |
| Auth | 10 req/min |
| Read operations | 50 req/min |
| Write operations | 20 req/min |
| Keyword generation | 10 req/min |
| Content generation | 5 req/min |
| Indexing | 20 req/min |
| Agent runs | 10 req/min |
| Agent wizard | 20 req/min |
| Agent CRUD | 30 req/min |
| Agent metrics | 10 req/min |
| Client logs | 10 req/min |
| Analytics reads | 30 req/min |
| Analytics writes | 10 req/min |
| Analytics reports | 20 req/min |
| Analytics realtime | 10 req/min |
| Analytics events | 10 req/min |

## Response Format

All endpoints return a standard wrapper (except webhooks):

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": { ... },
  "msg": "Operation completed successfully"
}
```

get.description:
Returns the current health status of the API and its dependencies (database connectivity, etc.).

- **Auth:** None required
- **Rate limit:** 100 req/min

post.description:
Authenticate with an App API key and receive a JWT app token.

- **Auth:** None — this is the entry point for obtaining tokens
- **Rate limit:** 10 req/min per client, plus a ceiling per app key
- The returned `access_token` must be sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on all protected endpoints
- Token expires after the time indicated in `expires_in` (seconds)

get.description:
List the authenticated user's generated articles — i.e. completed content-generation jobs — newest first. Powers the dashboard 'articles published' KPI, which buckets `created_at` by month.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 50 req/min

Items are capped at the 1000 most recent; `total` is the exact count.

**cURL example:**
```bash
curl https://api.1platform.pro/api/v1/posts \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $APP_TOKEN" \
  -H "x-user-token: $USER_TOKEN"
```

401.description: Authentication failed — invalid or missing token

post.description:
Analyze a domain and extract SEO keywords using AI-powered search analysis. Requires an active App with an AI provider configured.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 10 req/min

**Process:**
1. Analyzes domain content and structure
2. Extracts relevant keywords via search providers
3. Uses 1Platform AI to detect keyword cannibalization
4. Categorizes keywords by search intent and volume
5. Returns structured keyword data with metrics

**cURL example:**
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.1platform.pro/api/v1/posts/keywords/ \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $APP_TOKEN" \
  -H "x-user-token: $USER_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"domain": "example.com", "country": "es", "lang": "en"}'
```

401.description: Authentication failed — invalid or missing token

404.description: Billing record not found for user

429.description: Rate limit exceeded or plan limit reached

post.description:
Discover SEO keywords for a topic or theme using search analysis. Returns deduplicated keywords with estimated volume.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 10 req/min

**Process:**
1. Searches topic in search engines to discover top niche domains
2. Analyzes each domain for topic-relevant pages
3. Extracts main keyword from each page title via AI
4. Removes semantic duplicates (cannibalization)
5. Returns structured keyword data with estimated volume

401.description: Authentication failed — invalid or missing token

404.description: Billing record not found for user

429.description: Rate limit exceeded or plan limit reached

post.description:
Submit an async content generation job for a target keyword. Returns immediately with a job ID. Use `GET /content/jobs/{job_id}` to poll status. Requires AI and image provider keys configured in the App.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 5 req/min (AI-intensive)

**Process (runs in background):**
1. Generates title variations via 1Platform AI
2. Searches related content using search providers
3. Produces structured article with headings and paragraphs
4. Fetches relevant images from the configured image library
5. Creates a URL-friendly slug
6. Classifies content into provided categories

**cURL example:**
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.1platform.pro/api/v1/posts/content/ \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $APP_TOKEN" \
  -H "x-user-token: $USER_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"keyword": "best running shoes", "lang": "en", "image_provider": "default", "categories": ["sports"]}'
```

post.description:
Authenticate with a user API key and receive a JWT user token.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` only (no user token needed)
- **Rate limit:** 10 req/min
- The returned token must be sent as the `x-user-token` header on all user-scoped requests
- Token expires after the time indicated in `expires_in` (seconds)

**cURL example:**
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.1platform.pro/api/v1/users/token \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $APP_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"apiKey": "sk-user-api-key"}'
```

Register a new user with automatic billing and subscription setup.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` only (no user token needed)
- **Rate limit:** 20 req/min
- Creates a User, Billing (balance=0 USD), and Subscription (Free Plan)
- Returns the user's `api_key` used to obtain user tokens via `POST /api/v1/users/token`

**cURL example:**
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.1platform.pro/api/v1/users \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $APP_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"email": "user@example.com"}'
```

get.description:
Retrieve the authenticated user's profile information.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 50 req/min
- Returns id, username, email, is_active, and created_at

Retrieve billing balance and active subscription data for the authenticated user.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 50 req/min
- Returns balance, currency, and active subscription details

Retrieve available website categories for content classification.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 50 req/min
- Filter by status: `active` (default), `inactive`, or `all`

post.description:
Register a new website for the authenticated user.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 20 req/min
- Validates URL uniqueness per user
- Optionally enriches the website with an AI-generated description

**cURL example:**
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.1platform.pro/api/v1/users/websites \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $APP_TOKEN" \
  -H "x-user-token: $USER_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"url": "https://myblog.com", "category_id": "<objectId>", "lang": "es"}'
```

400.description: Validation error

409.description: Website already exists for this user

get.description:
Search for a website by its URL among the authenticated user's websites.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 50 req/min
- Pass the URL as a query parameter: `?url=https://example.com`

patch.description:
Update an existing website for the authenticated user.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 20 req/min
- Only the website owner can update it
- All fields are optional (partial update)
- Use this endpoint to set or update the `category_id`

**cURL example:**
```bash
curl -X PATCH https://api.1platform.pro/api/v1/users/websites/<WEBSITE_ID> \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $APP_TOKEN" \
  -H "x-user-token: $USER_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"category_id": "<objectId>", "site_name": "Updated Name"}'
```

get.description:
Retrieve details of a specific website by its ID.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 50 req/min
- Only returns websites owned by the authenticated user

delete.description:
Remove a website from the authenticated user's account.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 20 req/min
- Only the website owner can delete it
- This action is irreversible

get.description:
Paginated list of the websites registered by the authenticated user.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 50 req/min
- Only returns websites owned by the authenticated user
- Deleted websites are excluded

This is the collection listing. To look a single site up by its URL use `GET /users/websites?url=<url>`, which answers with one website or 404.

post.description:
Run the site's setup again and refresh its status.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 20 req/min
- Free: nothing is charged.
- Safe to repeat: steps that already succeeded are skipped, so nothing is created twice and no email is sent again.
- A site that is already working is never downgraded by a failed check.

Add or verify a website in the link-building marketplace.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 20 req/min
- **Actions:** `add` (register website) or `verify` (confirm ownership)
- The user must have marketplace credentials configured
- After adding, verify ownership to activate the listing

400.description: Invalid action, missing credentials, or verification failed

post.description:
Add, verify, delete a website or manage sitemaps in Google Search Console.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 20 req/min
- **Actions:** `add`, `verify`, `delete`, `sitemaps`
- The website must be registered in the platform before adding to Search Console
- For `sitemaps` action, include a `payload.sitemaps` array with sitemap URLs
- `sitemaps` requires ownership to be verified first; before that it returns 412 without charging
- `add` accepts an optional `verification_method` (`FILE`, the default, or `META`). `META` is only available for sites 1Platform serves, because it publishes the tag on the site itself; asking for it on any other site returns 409 without charging.
- Requires a Google service account with Search Console access

example.msg: Website verified successfully in Search Console

400.description: Invalid action or website not registered in Search Console

409.description: Meta-tag verification asked for a site 1Platform does not serve, or a method conflict with the stored one

412.description: Sitemaps submitted before ownership verification — verify the website first

get.summary: Get aggregate search performance across every website
get.description:
Retrieve one report that sums the search performance of ALL the caller's websites: 4 KPIs (clicks, impressions, CTR, average position) with a delta vs. the immediately preceding period of equal length, plus a daily series of how the total moved.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 20 req/min
- **Free** — a read-only report, never charged
- A site registered twice counts ONCE. `coverage` says how many properties the totals cover, how many documents were folded into another, and how many sites cannot contribute yet
- Served entirely from the figures 1Platform has stored and refreshes in the background; this endpoint never fetches anything live, so a site that has never synchronised is counted rather than loaded
- `end_date` is the most recent day that HAS data, which can be yesterday even when the report is requested today

get.summary: Get Search Console performance for a website
get.description:
Retrieve a Search Console performance report for a verified website: 4 KPIs (clicks, impressions, CTR, average position) with a delta vs. the immediately preceding period of equal length, a daily trend, and the first 25 queries/pages/countries by clicks.

- Each breakdown also reports how many distinct keys it HAS for the period (`queries_total`, `pages_total`, `countries_total`), so a table that ends at 25 can be told apart from one that was cut at 25. Rows beyond the first 25, and any other ordering, come from `GET /users/websites/{website_id}/searchconsole/performance/{dimension}`
- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 20 req/min
- **Free** — unlike add/verify/delete/sitemaps, this is a read-only report and is never charged
- Served from the figures 1Platform has stored, refreshed periodically in the background; `last_synced_at` says when. A site that has never been synchronised is loaded on this first request and answers a little slower
- Requires the website to already be verified in Search Console (409 otherwise)

404.description: Website not found or does not belong to user

409.description: Website is not verified in Search Console yet

429.description: Rate limit exceeded, or Search Console quota exceeded upstream

get.summary: Page through one Search Console breakdown table
get.description:
One page of a single performance breakdown — queries, pages or countries — for the same window the performance report covers.

The report itself already carries the first 25 rows of all three by clicks, so opening the panel still costs one request. This answers the rows beyond those, and every ordering other than clicks descending.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 50 req/min
- **Free** — a read of figures already stored, never charged
- **`sort` decides which rows the page contains, not just their order.** Ordering the first 25 by clicks and then re-sorting those does not produce the top rows by impressions; asking for `sort=impressions` here does
- `total` is how many distinct keys 1Platform has STORED for the period. It is not what Google holds: figures are kept per day up to a ceiling, and Search Console never discloses the queries it anonymises, so a breakdown can legitimately account for fewer clicks than the KPI above it
- Rows are ordered by `sort` and then by their key ascending. The tiebreaker is part of the contract, not an implementation detail: offset paging over an unstable order silently repeats and drops rows, and ties are the normal case here (dozens of keys at one click each)
- Served entirely from stored figures — paging never calls Search Console, so a site that has never synchronised answers with an empty page rather than spending quota
- Requires the website to already be verified in Search Console (409 otherwise)

get.summary: Get sitemap health for a website
get.description:
Retrieve the website's sitemaps with what Search Console actually reports about each one: URLs read and indexed, warnings, errors, and when Google last fetched it — beyond 1Platform's own record of having submitted them.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 20 req/min
- **Free** — read-only, never charged
- Degrades gracefully: when the site is not verified yet or Search Console cannot be reached, `google_status_available` is `false` and the rows carry 1Platform's submission state only

post.summary: Generate legal pages for a website
post.description:
Generate all legal pages for a website: privacy policy, cookie policy, legal notice, contact page, and about-me page.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 20 req/min
- Template-based pages use static HTML with variable substitution
- Contact and about-me pages are generated via 1Platform AI
- Requires an active App with AI provider configured

put.description:
Called by the SITE's own plugin, never the dashboard — a full replace, not a merge (WPG-02).

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Header:** `X-Site-URL` — disambiguates between two sites of the same owner; it is NOT proof of identity (D-11)
- **Rate limit:** 20 req/min

post.summary: Order an action on one of the site's plugins
post.description:
Dashboard-only (D-20): the `sk-` token installed on a site may list, claim and report its own orders, never create one. Repeating an identical live order is not an error — it returns the SAME order with 200 (WPG-05).

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>` of a verified dashboard user
- **Rate limit:** 20 req/min, keyed per (credential, website)

403.description: Dashboard verification required

409.description: Plugin already installed

422.description: Invalid or missing target, self-target, or not in inventory

429.description: Rate limit exceeded, or quota of live orders exceeded

get.summary: List plugin orders for a website
get.description:
Polled by the site every minute (filtering `status=pending`) and read by the dashboard panel (unfiltered).

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 50 req/min, keyed per (credential, website)

schema.description: Number of orders to skip, for pagination.

patch.description:
One transition per call, gated by the order's state machine and a CAS (WPG-05/06/08/10): `claimed` (the site claims it), `applied`/`failed` (the site reports the result), `cancelled` (the owner gives up on it).

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 20 req/min, keyed per (credential, website)

409.description: Not a valid transition from the current status

get.summary: Search the WordPress plugin directory / check abandonment
get.description:
One endpoint behind one cache-aside provider (D-8/D-9): with `q`, a text search against the directory for WPG-10's install dialog, each hit flagged with whether it is already on this site; without `q`, `abandoned` maps the site's OWN currently-reported plugin slugs to the directory's last release date, for every one that crossed the configured maintenance window (WPG-09). A directory outage degrades to empty results / an empty map, never a 500.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 50 req/min

patch.summary: Enable, disable, or apportion automatic catalog publishing for a website (ACA-05)
patch.description:
Turn automatic publishing on/off for a website served by a 1Platform tenant (Atlas), and set its monthly budget / catalog kinds / item cap.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 20 req/min
- Only the website owner can change it
- The website must already be served by a tenant (`atlas_tenant_slug` set), otherwise this responds `409 WEBSITE_NOT_A_TENANT`
- `unit_price_usd_override` cannot be set here — it is staff-only via `PATCH /platform/websites/{id}/autopublish/price`; sending it responds `422 AUTOPUBLISH_FIELD_NOT_WRITABLE` and applies nothing

**cURL example:**
```bash
curl -X PATCH https://api.1platform.pro/api/v1/users/websites/<WEBSITE_ID>/autopublish \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $APP_TOKEN" \
  -H "x-user-token: $USER_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"enabled": true, "kinds": ["book"], "monthly_budget_usd": "5.00", "max_items_per_cycle": 200}'
```

409.description: Website is not served by a tenant

422.description: Validation error, or an attempt to set unit_price_usd_override

503.description: Could not propagate the change to the serving product

get.summary: Current period consumption for a website's automatic publishing (ACA-05)
get.description:
Read-only period consumption for the website owner: how much of the current month's grant has been used. Never drives a charge.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 50 req/min
- All fields are `null` until the grant loop's first tick for this site

post.description:
Generate realistic fictional comments using AI for website content seeding.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 5 req/min
- Each comment includes a fictional author name and content text
- All comments are generated in a single AI request
- Requires an active App with AI provider configured

**cURL example:**
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.1platform.pro/api/v1/users/generations/comments \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $APP_TOKEN" \
  -H "x-user-token: $USER_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"count": 5, "lang": "es", "context": "Blog de tecnología"}'
```

400.description: Invalid input or AI generation failed

post.description:
Generate images using a configurable AI provider.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 5 req/min
- Each image is generated individually; partial results are returned if some attempts fail
- Image metadata is persisted for each generation
- Requires an active App with AI provider configured

200.description: Images generated successfully (may include partial results)

post.description:
Generate a complete profile card for a person using AI.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 5 req/min
- Includes gender detection, bio generation, social media discovery, and profile image retrieval
- Provide the person's name as `owner`; optional `context` enriches the bio
- Requires AI, search, and image provider keys in the App configuration

data.bio: Maria Garcia is a software engineer specializing in AI.

400.description: Missing or invalid owner name

post.description:
Revoke all existing JWT tokens for the authenticated user.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 10 req/min
- Increments the user's `token_version`, invalidating all previously issued tokens
- After calling this endpoint, the user must obtain a new token via `POST /api/v1/users/token`

**cURL example:**
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.1platform.pro/api/v1/users/revoke-tokens \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $APP_TOKEN" \
  -H "x-user-token: $USER_TOKEN"
```

get.description:
Every credential issued to the caller, masked. The secret is never here: it is shown once, when it is issued, and only its hash is kept.

post.summary: Show one of my tokens, once
post.description:
Shows the secret of one of the caller's own credentials for the only time it can be shown. The two kinds reach that promise by opposite routes, and the endpoint is the same:

- **App token** (`ak-`): the secret is GENERATED here. It exists nowhere before this call, which is how the administrator who approved the grant is unable to have seen it, and only its hash exists after.
- **User token** (`sk-`): the secret already exists and nothing is rotated — integrations presenting it keep working. Only available while nobody has looked yet AND the value is still recoverable, which is what `secret_recoverable` on the listing reports. A token minted through the panel handed its secret back at creation and kept only a SHA-256; it answers `credential_secret_unrecoverable` (409), and the way to get a usable one is to create a new token.

Only the owner can call this, and a second call is a 409.

**Auth:** app token + user token.

409.description: Already revealed (`credential_already_revealed`), never stored (`credential_secret_unrecoverable`) or revoked (`credential_revoked`)

post.description:
Create a new payment transaction and receive a checkout URL.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 20 req/min
- Payment is processed via the integrated payment service
- Returns a `payment_url` where the user completes checkout
- Transaction starts with status `CREATED`; status updates arrive via webhook
- Optional `return_url`: where the payer's browser lands after checkout. HTTPS, and its host must be registered via `POST /webhooks/config/domains`. Two variables are substituted into it, URL-encoded: `{{transaction_id}}` and `{{merchant_reference}}`. It is a redirect, not a notification — the webhook is still the only thing that settles an order
- Optional `branch_id`: charge on behalf of a commerce's BRANCH, in **that commerce's currency**. A branch and not a commerce because the branch is the unit the invoicing API already speaks — an invoice certifies under ITS establishment code — so an integration that emits invoices already holds one. Without it the currency comes from your primary balance, which misprices every commerce that trades in another one

**cURL example:**
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.1platform.pro/api/v1/users/transactions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $APP_TOKEN" \
  -H "x-user-token: $USER_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"amount": 25.00, "currency": "USD", "description": "Credit purchase"}'
```

**Charging in a commerce's currency (naming its branch):**
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.1platform.pro/api/v1/users/transactions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $APP_TOKEN" \
  -H "x-user-token: $USER_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"amount": 449.99, "branch_id": "6a5f8e7d93f925bfb527997a", "description": "Subscription INV-2026-10"}'
```

400.description: Invalid request data. Also returned when `return_url`'s host is not registered for this App — register it via `POST /webhooks/config/domains` (DNS verification is not required) — and when `customer_email` is not a well-formed address. Both are checked before the payment provider is contacted, so a rejected request leaves no checkout session behind.

404.description: Billing record not found for user. post.description:
Receive transaction status updates from the payment service. This endpoint carries no Bearer authentication and is invoked by the external payment provider. The provider does NOT sign its callbacks, so authenticity rests on a shared secret that 1Platform generates and an operator installs on the provider side; the provider returns it as an `X-Webhook-Token` header or a `?token=` query parameter. Verification is fail-closed (401) only while `payments.webhook_auth_enforced` is true; until that cutover the endpoint accepts unverified callbacks and merely logs the verdict the check would have reached. Processing is idempotent — duplicate webhooks are safely ignored to prevent double-charging — and the endpoint always returns HTTP 200 to suppress aggressive provider retries. Rate limit: 20 req/min.

**Flow:**
1. Extract `externalId` from the root payload to find the local transaction
2. Check idempotency (if status unchanged, return success)
3. Validate status transition
4. Update transaction status
5. If approved, credit the user's balance

**Response format** (simple JSON, not ResponseWrapper):
```json
{"status": "success", "message": "Processed"}
```

delete.description:
Remove a business from the workspace by archiving it.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 20 req/min
- Requires the `admin` role on the business (or being an `app_admin` of its tenant)
- **Nothing is deleted.** The business is marked archived and every related document is preserved: invoices already certified, branches, user assignments, payment links, deliveries and terminal applications. Its invoices keep appearing in `GET /invoices` and in the tax report
- The business disappears from `GET /businesses` and `GET /admin/businesses`, stops accepting writes, and its `GET /businesses/{businessId}` still answers 200 with `archived: true` so a saved link can explain what happened
- Idempotent: archiving an already-archived business answers 200 and keeps the original timestamp
- The document number stays taken by the archived business; creating a new one with it answers 409 `business_nit_archived`
- **Payment links are NOT switched off unless you ask.** The public checkout resolves a link by its token and never loads the business, so a link issued before archiving stays payable. Pass `cancel_payment_links=true` to cancel the ones still charging; the response then carries `payment_links_cancelled` with what actually happened. Without the parameter the behaviour is unchanged
- `data.active_payment_links` reports the links still charging (`{count, totals}` per currency), so the caller can warn before archiving

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 5 req/min
- **Refuses when the domain already receives mail elsewhere:** `409` with `code: mail_foreign_mx`, and **no DNS record is written**. A mail exchanger at the apex carries all of the domain's mail, so publishing over an existing one would intercept correspondence the merchant already relies on.
- **`503 mail_mx_unverifiable`:** public DNS could not be reached. Distinct from `409` on purpose — 'there is nothing there' and 'I could not find out' are different answers, and treating the second as the first would write records on a domain nobody checked.
- **Not yet delegated:** an external domain whose nameservers are not ours is created in `awaiting_delegation`. That is a state, not an error.

delete.summary: Switch business mail off for a whole domain
delete.description:
Stop using this domain for mail, and leave the DNS and the conversations in a correct state (COR-07 CA-2).

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`
- **Rate limit:** 5 req/min, shared with the address writes
- **Order matters.** The `MX` is retired FIRST, so mail that arrives after the addresses are gone is bounced to the sender rather than accepted and dropped. Then the conversations are frozen read-only — never deleted: the correspondence is the merchant's business record and stays readable, what stops is replying. Then each address is retired through the same path a single deactivation takes, so adding the same address again later still works.
- **A zone we can no longer edit is not a failure.** That is the expiry/transfer case: the DNS errors are counted and reported, and the teardown finishes anyway. Refusing would leave the addresses live in our database for a name the merchant no longer controls.
- **Idempotent.** A domain that never had mail answers `200` with `skipped: no_mail_domain`.

- **Always served as `application/octet-stream` with an `attachment` disposition**, never as the type the sender declared. Honouring a sender-declared `text/html` would turn a signed download into attacker-authored HTML hosted under our own signature.
- An attachment on somebody else's conversation answers `404`.

post.description:
The transport delivers one message here.

- **Auth:** an HMAC over `route_token + timestamp + body`, in `x-mail-signature`, with the epoch seconds in `x-mail-timestamp`. The signature covers the ROUTE as well as the body: without that, a body signed for one merchant replays against another merchant's URL and verifies, so the routing itself would be unauthenticated.
- **Rate limit:** one shared bucket keyed by route token.
- **`403` before any parse.** A malformed body with a bad signature answers `403`, not `400`: a `400` would prove hostile input was parsed before it was authenticated.
- **`413` measured on the stream**, not on `Content-Length` — a chunked request does not carry that header.
- **Idempotent.** A second delivery of the same message answers `200`, creates nothing and notifies nobody. The provider retries on purpose.
- Automatic replies, list traffic and null-sender bounces are dropped.

403.description: Signature verification failed

post.summary: Receive a delivery or bounce event
post.description:
Moves an outbound message from `sent` to its confirmed outcome.

- **Auth:** the same HMAC over `route_token + timestamp + body`.
- **Rate limit:** shares the inbound bucket.
- **Idempotent:** correlated by the provider's own message id, so a repeated event writes the same value. A late duplicate of an earlier success does not walk a bounced message back to delivered.
- `sent` is never rendered as `delivered` without one of these.

get.summary: Subscription handshake for an inbound channel URL (server-to-server)
get.description:
The one-time check a messaging provider runs against a callback URL before it will deliver to it: it presents the value the operator configured and expects the challenge echoed back verbatim.

- **Auth:** the verification value configured on the application, compared in constant time. It is the only request on this door that carries no signature, so that comparison IS the authentication.
- **Body:** the challenge as `text/plain`, not JSON. A client generated from a spec that documented it as JSON would send back a quoted string and the provider would refuse the subscription.
- **Rate limit:** 300 req/min per inbound token.
- An unknown token answers `404` and a wrong verification value `403` — different on purpose: the first says "this URL was never ours", the second says "this URL is ours and you did not prove you may use it".

One signed delivery from a connected messaging account, turned into stored conversation.

- **Auth:** an HMAC over the RAW bytes with the signing secret of the application the URL belongs to, in `X-Hub-Signature-256`. Verified before the payload is parsed at all; anything else answers `403` and writes nothing.
- **Routing:** `{inbound_token}` names the application. The concrete channel is resolved afterwards, from the account the SIGNED payload names — never from anything the caller asserts.
- **Size:** bodies over the configured ceiling answer `413`, checked against the declared length before a byte is buffered.
- **Rate limit:** 300 req/min per inbound token. On the platform's shared application that bucket is common to every workspace on it, by construction.
- **Kill switch:** a workspace with `sales.enabled` off answers `ignored` and runs no turn. On an application that workspace owns nothing is stored either; on the shared application the message is still stored, because which workspace it belongs to is only known after it is parsed.
- Always answers `200` once authenticated — for a delivery that carried no message, one for an account nobody has connected, and a redelivery of one already stored. `status` says only whether anything was written; it never reports which accounts were recognised, which would make this endpoint an enumeration oracle for a caller who cannot be identified.

post.summary: Create the reservation charge for a lead
post.description:
Creates — or returns, if it already exists — this prospect's reservation charge, and answers with a 1Platform link to share.

**The body is empty and that is the design.** The amount, the currency, the concept and the destination all come from the offer this workspace configured: there is no field to put a price in, so no caller — a person or the agent — can discount, round or invent one.

Idempotent by the lead itself, not by a read: asked three times it answers the same URL three times, and simultaneous callers resolve to one charge rather than to whoever wrote last.

A lead with no channel CAN be charged — a sale closed on the phone with the link sent by hand is legitimate — and is recorded as such so the funnel report can tell it apart from one the agent closed.

get.summary: The funnel, the wins and what they cost
get.description:
Leads by stage, by channel and by origin over a date range, the wins, and the tokens the conversations spent.

**A win is `won_at`, never the stage.** A stage is editable — its definition lives on the offer — so a report derived from it would let renaming a funnel rewrite history: leads that paid would stop counting and leads that never paid would start.

**`wins` is a LIST and never a single figure.** `payment` is a sale a credited charge proved; `manual` is one a person asserted. They are reported apart because one is evidence and the other is a claim, and the amounts are grouped by currency because two currencies do not add.

The window is on when the LEAD ARRIVED, for every figure including the wins: it answers "of the prospects who reached us in this period, how many bought". Omitted, it is the last 30 days; wider than a year, it is clamped rather than refused.

get.summary: What the panel needs to open the account-connection dialog
get.description:
Workspace admins only. Returns PUBLIC values plus a single-use handshake bound to this workspace and good for minutes — no credential, nothing that signs anything: the exchange happens server-side precisely so none of that has to travel through a browser.

`dialog_url` is composed SERVER-side and is the field the panel opens: this side knows which application asks, against which API version and presenting which configuration, and the handshake has to be inside the URL for the redemption to be tied back to this workspace.

`enabled: false` with every other field null is the honest answer when the flow cannot run — the vertical is off, the deployment has no shared application, or no dialog can be composed here — rather than identifiers for a dialog whose redemption is guaranteed to fail. No handshake is minted in that case either.

post.summary: Redeem the dialog's one-time code and connect the account
post.description:
Workspace admins only, and 201 because it mints a channel.

The handshake is validated and CONSUMED first, atomically and bound to this workspace, before the code is redeemed anywhere: without that step the flow is an OAuth with no CSRF protection, and an attacker who authorises their own account can get an authenticated browser to attach it to somebody else's CRM. Missing, expired, already spent and issued elsewhere are one answer — 400 — because telling them apart draws the map being probed for.

Which accounts the credential actually covers is read from the credential, never from the request. Every step before persistence writes NOTHING, so a failure leaves no half-connected channel — the state that looks connected, receives nothing, and tells the operator nothing about which step failed.

`offer_id` is OPTIONAL: the dialog hands the browser a code and a handshake and nothing else, so a workspace with exactly one active offer gets that funnel. A workspace with several is asked to name one — which funnel a stranger's messages enter decides the stages, the questions and the reservation amount they meet, and there is no default for that.

Paginated, newest first. Every row says WHETHER a credential, a signing secret and a verification value are stored, and none of them says what they are — not even as ciphertext.

No row carries the inbound URL. The URL belongs to the application and not to the channel, so repeating it per row says nothing new, and a list is the shape most likely to be rendered for a reader who is not an administrator. The single-channel read is where an administrator fetches it.

post.summary: Connect an account by pasting its credentials
post.description:
Workspace admins only. The fallback path, for a workspace that runs its OWN provider application; the assisted dialog is the ordinary way in and never puts a credential in a browser.

`channel_app_id` is REQUIRED here and must name the workspace's own application: pasting an account is a claim on a key that routes inbound messages platform-wide, and nothing on this path proves the caller controls the account it names. The assisted flow proves it — it reads the accounts the redeemed credential actually covers — so on the platform's shared application that flow is the only way in, and this route answers 403 `channel_account_not_granted`.

The account is unique across the whole platform — it is the key an inbound message is attributed by, so two workspaces claiming one account would make a message belong to both. One already connected answers 409 and says nothing about who holds it: naming them would leak that the account exists here, and the other workspace's channel is never overwritten.

Secrets are stored encrypted and are never returned in any shape.

The caller names an **event** from a closed enum and supplies its typed parameters. The server resolves the template, its language and the recipients from configuration, renders every parameter itself, and asks the provider to accept the message.

**`202` does not mean delivered.** The provider confirms that it validated the request's structure; delivery is only ever reported through a webhook, which this surface does not have. `accept_status` is the provider's own word, verbatim.

The body carries no recipient, no scope, no template and no free text — each of those is resolved server-side on purpose.

Send the same `idempotency_key` twice and the second call answers `202` with `accept_status: "duplicate"` and sends nothing. Derive the key from the caller's **spacing window**, never from the instant.

get.summary: Load the heatmap collector for a site (public)
get.description:
Serves the JavaScript collector for one site. This is what a site installs by pasting a single async script tag into its page head; everything else — sampling, listeners, route changes, batching and sending — happens inside the returned script.

- **Auth:** none. The path carries a stable, non-guessable ADDRESS, not a credential.
- **Always `200`, never `404`.** An unknown address, a site switched off and a site over its monthly ceiling all return an inert body: a 404 in a customer's console is a support ticket, and it would confirm which addresses exist.
- **Cached privately** for 5 minutes with an `ETag`, so a repeat visit revalidates instead of re-reading configuration. `private` and not `public`: the body embeds this site's capture credential, and a shared cache holding it would also keep serving it after a rotation.
- **Rate limit:** per site address and client network.

post.summary: Send a batch of heatmap samples (public)
post.description:

- **Auth:** none. The capture token in the path is the capability.
- **Content type: `text/plain`**, deliberately. That keeps the request SIMPLE so the browser sends no preflight; the server reads the raw body and parses it itself.
- Answers `202` whenever the token exists — including when the site is switched off or over its ceiling, which the browser cannot act on and which distinguishing would turn into an oracle.
- A path that matches none of the site's declared route patterns is counted as discarded and never stored.

get.summary: Which telemetry tag a store of ours should inject
get.description:
Lo llama el **servidor** de nuestros productos (hoy `bower-dashboard`) para inyectar la etiqueta sin que el comerciante toque código.

Se resuelve **por petición**: un despliegue sirve N tiendas y cada una recibe SU dirección. Una dirección horneada en la imagen sería una sola para cada tienda, y en telemetría eso significa los errores de muchas en el panel de una.

Devuelve `tag: null` cuando no corresponde — host sin propiedad probada, canal apagado, vertical apagada o proyecto bloqueado— y ése es el caso normal de la mayoría de las peticiones.

La **credencial no viaja por acá**: vive dentro del script, que es lo que permite rotarla sin que ninguna tienda vuelva a desplegar.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` (sin token de usuario)
- **Rate limit:** 120 req/min. El techo asume que el llamador CACHEA por host: una petición por host y por vida de caché desde cada contenedor de tienda, no una por render.

- **Auth:** App token (`Authorization: Bearer <app_token>`)
- **Rate limit:** 10/min per client IP at this endpoint. A separate, silent limit of 3 emails per 10 minutes per recipient is enforced one layer down, in the email-delivery engine: past that ceiling this endpoint still returns 200 (by design, see below) but the email is not sent.
- Always responds 200 with an empty envelope to avoid email enumeration — including when the per-recipient send limit above was hit, so retrying quickly for the same address will not surface the throttle.

Provisions a new tenant App: creates the App record, seeds a DashboardConfig, default roles, and an admin user pinned to the supplied email; turns the tenant's dashboard on and emails its administrator. Returns the new App including its api_key (staff-only, shown once) and `keys_configured` — which provider credentials are set, never their values.

`admin_mode: "adopt"` resolves the administrator to an account that already exists and MOVES it — with its tenant-scoped resources — into the new tenant. Omitting the field keeps the previous behaviour exactly, including the 409 on a taken address.

A `null` in place of a namespace removes the namespace; a `null` in place of a setting removes that setting. This is a DIFFERENT axis from `GET /platform/features`, and the two are easy to confuse: that one is the dashboard's module rail and writes `App.config.<namespace>.enabled`, while these are agent tool permissions and live in `App.config.features.<flag>`. Switching a module on does not grant a tool, and granting a tool does not put a section in anyone's sidebar.

Write them through `PATCH /platform/apps/{app_id}` with `config_patch: {"features": {"<flag>": true}}` — the `features` namespace accepts booleans only.

post.description:
`Agent.tools` es un arreglo persistido en el documento del agente, no el registro de tools. El bucle de corrida arma lo que se le ofrece al modelo **y** lo que el despacho permite a partir de ese arreglo, así que una tool nueva es **invisible e inejecutable** para cualquier agente creado antes de que existiera.

Esta operación sólo **agrega**: no quita tools, no reordena y no reescribe definiciones existentes. Es idempotente, y respeta una tool que el dueño haya quitado a propósito. Lo que el plan del inquilino no habilita no se agrega, y cada omisión viene con su motivo — un tope silencioso se leería como que no quedó nada afuera.

Usar `dry_run` primero.

get.description:
The tenant × feature matrix, with the effective value and — the point of the screen — **where it came from**. Today no tenant in production has any of these keys written, so every one of them is inheriting and nothing surfaces that.

`operable` answers whether the vertical's provider-backed path can run right now. A feature can legitimately be `enabled: true, operable: false`: switching it on before contracting the provider is a normal order of operations, and the vertical answers its own typed error until then.

This response is a **projection**. It never carries `App.config`, which holds tenant mail credentials in plain text.

⚠️ `source: "platform"` reflects the `PlatformSettings` snapshot taken at boot: `ConfigProvider` loads it once, so a value edited straight in Mongo shows up here only after a restart.

⚠️ `enforcement` is the one field to read before trusting a switch. Only `ads` resolves the tenant's own App, so only its switch blocks that tenant's users. `deliveries` and `trading` gate on `current_app.config` — the App of the BEARER TOKEN — so switching either off for a tenant that is not the caller's own App removes the module from that tenant's menu and blocks nothing server-side.

patch.summary: Switch one feature on or off for one tenant (staff)
patch.description:
Writes the single leaf `App.config.<namespace>.enabled` with a targeted `$set`, so a vertical's other settings — spending ceilings, provider, windows — are left exactly as they are.

Three operations, not two:

- `{"enabled": true}` switches on
- `{"enabled": false}` switches off **explicitly** (`source` becomes `app`)
- `{"enabled": null}` **removes** the override so the tenant inherits again

An empty body is **422**: a request that says nothing must not read as a successful change.

The tenant cannot undo this. Every namespace in the catalogue is in `_PROTECTED_CONFIG_KEYS`, so `PATCH /admin/app` answers 400 for it.

⚠️ The switch is per **App**, and `GET /dashboard/bootstrap` resolves the App of the *token*, not of the user — so flipping a feature on the App the dashboard front-end itself authenticates with reaches every one of its users at once.

**Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` (console workspace) + `x-user-token: <staff_token>`

get.description:
How the workspace's agent runs ended over a period: the totals with their breakdown, the same breakdown per agent, and the most recent failures — so a broken agent is found before the tenant reports it.

The arithmetic closes: the total is the SUM of the outcomes, and a run still in flight is counted apart, never as a failure. The success rate is measured over FINISHED runs only, for the same reason.

**Failure reasons are redacted.** What a run stores is the raw text of the exception that ended it, which routinely quotes whatever an external call answered. Credentials, addresses, network locations and vendor names are removed on the way out; this endpoint never serves the stored text.

**Retention is declared, not implied.** Run records are deleted after the number of days in `retention_days`, so a period that starts before `retention_cutoff` comes back with `period_predates_retention: true` and its counts are incomplete BY DESIGN — not evidence of a quiet period. get.description:
The archive of administrative actions, newest first, across **all** workspaces.

Filterable by subject workspace (`app_id`), actor (`actor_user_id`), `action` and an inclusive day range (`from`/`to`). The range is bounded server-side: at most **366 days**, and a range whose start is after its end is rejected instead of quietly matching nothing.

**The retention policy travels in the payload.** This archive has *no expiry* — `retention.policy` is `no_expiry` and `retention.records_begin_at` says how far back the data actually goes, so a window that predates the archive can be reported as such (`retention.range_predates_records`) instead of rendering an empty table that reads as *nothing happened*.

put.description:
Opens a new validity window and **closes the previous one first**.

That order is load-bearing: only one window may be live per workspace, so inserting before closing would collide with the window being replaced. Closed windows keep the prices they carried, which is what stops a plan change from restating a month that is already closed.

The window's own history is the record of the change — who set it, when, and what the previous one said.

A negative overage price is refused: it is the money path, and a negative unit price turns a bill into a credit.

post.description:
Runs the monthly close and reports, workspace by workspace, what happened.

**Idempotent.** Closing the same workspace-month twice leaves ONE period with the SAME amounts; the second attempt is reported as `skipped` and charges nothing — nothing is charged at all, this produces the calculation and its detail.

**A closed month is immutable.** The amounts are computed against a copy of the plan and of the prices taken at close time, so changing either afterwards cannot restate the month.

**One workspace failing never aborts the rest.** Each failure carries a bounded reason and can be retried on its own by naming it in `app_ids`. The arithmetic reconciles: `requested = ok + skipped + failed`.

Claims abandoned by a process that died are reclaimed before the run starts, so a month wedged mid-close is repaired by the same call that retries it.

Only a calendar month that has already finished can be closed, and only within the last 24 months.

Resolves the health of every integration for a page of workspaces in a SINGLE call — one bounded query per integration across the whole page, never one call per workspace.

Three answers are kept apart on purpose and never collapse into one another: `healthy` (measured, recently, and it worked), `no_signal` (nothing here can answer the question — the substrate records no outcome, the last one is too old to mean anything, or the probe itself did not run) and `not_configured` (the workspace never set this up). `degraded` and `failing` are reserved for integrations whose substrate can record a failure; when `failure_visible` is false, `healthy` is not a state that integration can reach, however good things look.

Richer than `GET /platform/metrics`, which returns four bare counters.

Three things this answer will not do:

- **It never adds two currencies together.** Amounts come back as a list, one entry per currency, because the amount stored on a ledger entry is denominated by the entry's own currency.
- **It never reports a percentage it did not measure.** `change_pct` is `null` when the previous window is zero, and an empty amount list means there were no entries at all — which is not the same as an amount of zero.
- **It never hides consumption it cannot attribute.** Entries whose workspace reference resolves to no workspace are counted in `unattributed_operations` and included in the amounts, so the figures still reconcile against what was actually charged.

`days` is capped at 90 and `top` at 25.

get.description:
Charged consumption over a bounded range, aggregated by workspace, by product operation, by currency and by day. Defaults to the current month when no range is given.

**Amounts are grouped by currency and never added across them.** The cost column of the ledger is not always denominated in the same currency, so a single 'total spend' number would be a sum of different things.

**Totals are the rounding of the sum, not the sum of roundings.** Each amount is accumulated at full precision and rendered once.

**`unattributed` is not an error bucket, it is money.** Some ledger entries carry a workspace reference that resolves to no workspace at all, while the amount on them was really debited. They are reported separately and included in `totals`, so the breakdown still adds up. Dropping them would under-count the period and look consistent doing it.

`by_workspace` is a page ranked by activity and capped by `limit`; `totals` always covers the whole range. `by_operation` folds anything past its display ceiling into an explicit `other` row, and entries with no operation key into `unclassified` — nothing is discarded.

The range is capped at 92 days and `limit` at 200.

get.summary: List the users of one workspace (staff)
get.description:
The people inside one workspace, with their roles and their state, so a support request can be answered without asking the customer to describe their own account.

**Read-only.** There is no create, edit, invite or remove on this surface.

**No credential of any kind is returned** — not the user's own key, not a token, not a hash. The payload is a declared allow-list rather than a redaction pass, so a field added to the user document later cannot leak through it.

The workspace is resolved from the **path**, never from the caller's token: the console authenticates as its own workspace while operating on somebody else's.

Results are bounded: 50 per page by default, 100 at most, `skip` capped, and `q` limited to 60 characters and matched literally.

**Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` (console workspace) + `x-user-token: <staff_token>`

**Rate limit:** 60 req/min

post.description:
Issues a new workspace credential and **retires the previous one in the same operation**. The old value stops authenticating as soon as this returns: integrations still presenting it are rejected on their next request. Warn the customer before calling this.

The new value appears in **this response and nowhere else, ever**. It is stored hashed, no later read reproduces it, and the audit entry records that the rotation happened without recording either value. A value that was not captured is replaced by rotating again.

**Refused for the workspace the caller is authenticated with** (`platform_credential_rotation_refused`, 409): completing that rotation would revoke the app token of the request performing it, and the same response that reported success would have locked the operator out. Any other workspace rotates normally.

Takes no request body — the subject is the workspace in the path. The console is expected to gate the action behind a typed confirmation of the workspace name and a warning about the clients that will break.

**Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` (console workspace) + `x-user-token: <staff_token>`

**Rate limit:** 60 req/min

get.summary: Limits in force for one workspace, and what they do not cover (staff)
get.description:
Every ceiling that is **actually enforced**, with the value the server compares against, the usage for the period and the remainder — resolved through the same reader the enforcing code uses, not re-derived here.

Two rules make this list trustworthy:

* A ceiling with no reader behind it is **not shown**. Painting one would put a knob on screen that changes nothing.
* A charge type that **no ceiling governs** is shown anyway, with `applies: false` and the reason. Omitting it silently would let an operator read coverage into a blank.

`limit: null` means no ceiling is declared. It is never `0` for that case, so an unlimited resource is never drawn as a full bar. `used: null` means usage is not measurable at the scope the ceiling is applied at — which happens when a ceiling is applied per user rather than per workspace.

`scope` says what the ceiling is counted over: this workspace, each user, or the whole platform. A platform-scoped row is shared with every other workspace, and is the reason an operation here can be refused while this workspace is nowhere near a ceiling of its own.

Amounts travel as decimal strings: the same row shape carries counts and money, and money sent as a JSON number arrives rounded.

**Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` (console workspace) + `x-user-token: <staff_token>`

**Rate limit:** 60 req/min

Everything minted through the panel handed its secret back at creation and kept only a SHA-256, and answers `credential_secret_unrecoverable` (409) — for those, re-issue.

Nothing is generated and nothing is rotated: whatever presents this token keeps working. What the call spends is the look, and a second call is a 409.

get.summary: What the merchant collected, by currency, plus what is still owed
get.description:
Collected, refunded, pending, blocked and awaiting reconciliation for the caller's businesses, **grouped by currency and never added across it**, with a DAILY series over the range.

**Flow and stock are not the same thing, and `scope` says which is which.** `collected`, `refunded` and `series` are bounded by `range`; `pending`, `blocked` and `needs_reconciliation` are balances of the instant. The last of those carries no date at all, so two consecutive monthly reports show the same amount and adding them counts it twice.

**The day is the TENANT's, not UTC.** A collection at 02:00Z belongs to the previous day in Guatemala, and `range.timezone` states the clock that was applied. The month-to-date figure on `/dashboard/summary` uses the UTC month of its two siblings instead, so at a month boundary the two can differ by the hours of the offset — they are not the same number and must not be presented as one.

**Money that came back is not money collected**, and a live link nobody can pay today is not pending revenue: both have their own field.

`no_visible_businesses` is NOT the same as having collected nothing. Zero is the normal state on day one, so the two must be labelled differently or the first can never be noticed.

**Range:** absolute `YYYY-MM-DD`, at most 366 days, defaulting to the last 30.

**Rate limit:** 20 req/min

**Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`

get.summary: The merchant's collections, filtered and paginated
get.description:
One page of collections. `pagination.total` is the filter's REAL count, not the length of `items`.

**`status` filters the EFFECTIVE status, not the stored one.** Expiry is applied lazily — a lapsed link keeps saying `active` in the database until a payer opens its URL — so filtering the stored value would have `?status=expired` omit every link that lapsed unopened while the payment links table three clicks away already shows them as expired.

**`date_field` says which date is being filtered**, because the answer changes the result completely: `paid_at` is null on every row that is not paid, so combining it with a status that can never be paid returns nothing BY CONSTRUCTION. That combination answers 422 `collections_date_field_conflict` rather than an empty page, which would be indistinguishable from a real result.

**`settlement` is what gives a summary figure a findable subject.** Without it a collection that needs reconciling lists as `cancelled`, the same as a cancellation that never held any money.

**`payer` is absent when unknown AND when the request arrives impersonating.** These reads stay reachable under a 'view as' session, and the buyer's address is not something an admin viewing as a merchant gets to read.

**Pagination:** `limit` at most 100; asking for more is a 422, never the whole set.

**Rate limit:** 50 req/min

**Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`

get.summary: Download the filtered collections report as CSV
get.description:
The rows behind `GET /collections`, under the SAME filter, as a CSV **streamed in batches** — the file is never built in memory.

**The file covers the FILTER, not the page.** Its row count matches the `total` the listing reports for the same filter; `X-Total-Rows` states it on the response.

Every amount carries its currency in the same row — there is no total column without one — and the date column names the basis it was filtered on. The status, the channel and the situation are written in the product's own vocabulary, never in a provider's, and no provider identifier travels in any cell.

**The payer column is dropped entirely under impersonation**, header and cells: an export is every address in the filter, in one attachment.

**It refuses rather than truncates.** Above 50000 rows it answers 422 `collections_export_too_large` with the count, so nobody reconciles against a silently short file.

Headers and values follow `Accept-Language` (`es` by default).

**Rate limit:** 20 req/min

**Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <app_token>` + `x-user-token: <user_token>`

AgentMemoryItemResponse.title: AgentMemoryItemResponse
AgentMemoryItemResponse.description:
One remembered item, as the owner's panel and the console read it — AMC-08.

Every field the client draws is declared HERE, because FastAPI discards a key
the response model does not name and does so in SILENCE: the value would be
right in the database, right on the dict the service returns, and absent from
the body — with every service-level test green (CA-6).

``subject_key`` is deliberately NOT published. It is internal, the model never
sees it, and it carries a normalised copy of somebody's search query that this
payload has no reason to hold.

AgentMemoryKind.title: AgentMemoryKind
AgentMemoryKind.description:
WHAT a remembered item is. Closed enum, on purpose (D-3).

What gets written here comes back into the opening turn of every following
run, so a poisoned memory PERSISTS. A record with a shape can be wrapped,
labelled and bounded; a free-form blob cannot.

AgentMemoryOrigin.title: AgentMemoryOrigin
AgentMemoryOrigin.description:
WHO wrote it, which is what decides how much the block trusts it.

The briefing wraps ``RUN`` and ``AGENT`` as untrusted data and ``OWNER`` as
instructions (D-3/D-11/D-14). The agent cannot write ``OWNER``: if it could,
it would grant itself the very faculty the owner uses to restrain it.

AgentMemoryOutcome.title: AgentMemoryOutcome
AgentMemoryOutcome.description:
How the applied thing turned out, in this domain's own words.

A mirror of ``AgentIntervention.measurement_status`` and NOT a copy of its
values: what reaches the model and the panel has to say "improved" or "not
measured", never ``pending``/``unmeasurable``. ``UNTRACKED`` and
``MEASURING`` are different states and AMC-04 CA-2 requires distinct labels:
the census found one pre-AEM-01 row with ``measurement_status = None`` that
will never be measured at all.

AgentMemoryStatus.title: AgentMemoryStatus
AgentMemoryStatus.description:
Whether an item still governs anything.

``ARCHIVED`` is not decoration. The cap of AMC-07 CA-4 has to evict, and the
other two candidate states both lie: ``RESOLVED`` tells the owner that a
pending item which was never applied is done, and ``FORGOTTEN`` applies of
its own accord the state D-16 reserves for the owner and declares
irreversible. ``ARCHIVED`` leaves the briefing and **keeps counting for the
guard** (A-15b): if eviction reset the counter, the agent would go back to
paying for the very target this epic exists to stop.

AgentMode.title: AgentMode
AgentMode.description:
What shape of work an agent does.

``TASK`` is every agent that exists today and is the default, so the field is
invisible to them: a document written before this enum existed reads back as
``task`` and takes exactly the path it took yesterday.

``CONVERSATIONAL`` is the sales vertical's mode. The difference is not
cosmetic — it changes three things the loop does: the history is seeded from
a persisted thread instead of a single input message, ``finish_task`` is
neither offered nor honoured (its result is an internal summary and the
reader here is a prospect on a messaging app), and the last iteration is
re-bound without tools so the run always ends with something to say.

AgentModelTier.title: AgentModelTier
AgentModelTier.description:
Neutral capacity tier an agent runs on (D-14, D-46, AGT-19 CA-3/CA-4).

Replaces the previous ``AllowedModel`` enum, whose members were COMMERCIAL
MODEL IDENTIFIERS living in the domain model and — through
``AgentResponse.model`` — travelling all the way to the client, which the
ecosystem's brand rule forbids outright.

The tier is a level of indirection, not a rename. It resolves to
``(provider, model identifier, output ceiling)`` in the PROTECTED ``models``
namespace of ``PlatformSettings`` (D-52), so repointing a tier at a different
engine is a configuration edit that touches neither the domain, nor the API
contract, nor a single price key — the tariffs are keyed by tier for exactly
that reason (AGT-19 CA-8).

AgentPersona.title: AgentPersona
AgentPersona.description:
How a conversational agent sounds to the person on the other side.

Every field is nullable and ``None`` means "the system default", which is
what makes VVO-05 CA-6 true without a migration: a workspace that never
opened this screen gets exactly the prompt, tone and tool palette it would
have got with no persona at all.

It travels through the RUN CONTEXT and is never written into the persisted
thread. That is the whole reason a change applies to the NEXT message rather
than to the next conversation: a persona baked into the history would freeze
the tone of every thread on the day it was first spoken.

AggregateCoverage.title: AggregateCoverage
AggregateCoverage.description:
How much of the user's estate the aggregate actually speaks for.

Every field counts in ONE unit and the four that partition the estate add
up to it: ``sites_counted + sites_duplicated + sites_never_synced +
sites_unverified == sites_total``. An earlier draft mixed the units —
``sites_counted`` counted PROPERTIES while its three siblings counted
DOCUMENTS — so the numbers came out at 26 + 4 + 5 = 35 over a total of 37
and nothing said where the missing two had gone. They were the duplicate
documents already folded into a property, which is what
``sites_duplicated`` now names.

``sites_blocked`` is a SUBSET of ``sites_never_synced`` rather than a fifth
part, so the partition is unaffected. It exists because the two states read
identically in the counter and could not be more different on screen:
measured across production, 23 of 23 sites that have never produced a figure
are not waiting for a first load at all — every one of them is failing it,
22-23 attempts deep. A block that counts them together can only say "still
gathering, they will show up on their own", which for those users is a
promise nothing is going to keep.

AppProvisionResponse.title: AppProvisionResponse
AppProvisionResponse.description:
The 201 of ``POST /platform/apps``.

Deliberately NOT ``AppFullResponse`` (#500): that base carries ``keys:
AppKeys`` verbatim, which put the Fernet ciphertext of eight provider
credentials (``AnalyticsKeys.client_secret_encrypted``,
``CloudflareKeys.api_token_encrypted``, ``AdsKeys.credential_encrypted``,
``WhatsAppKeys.credential_encrypted``,
``SearchConsoleKeys.service_account_json_encrypted``, and
``CourierKeys.credential_encrypted`` /``webhook_secret_encrypted``/
``notice_credential_encrypted``) — plus every plaintext one — on the wire
of the ONE route with this criterion; every other superadmin projection
(``AdminAppResponse``, ``AppInspectResponse``) already answers booleans
only. ``api_key`` still crosses here on purpose: unlike the provider
credentials, THIS is the one moment the workspace key is readable at all.

``admin`` and ``welcome_email`` exist HERE and not only in the dict the
service returns for a reason worth keeping: ``SuccessResponse[T].data`` is
validated by FastAPI on the way OUT, so any key ``T`` does not declare is
dropped in silence. Inventing these fields without declaring them answers a
flawless 201 that is missing exactly the report the screen needs.

ArchiveCancelReport.title: ArchiveCancelReport
ArchiveCancelReport.description:
What happened to the links when the business was archived.

INVARIANT: ``requested == cancelled + skipped + failed``.

Without ``skipped`` the arithmetic does not close: a link that gets PAID
between reading the ids and running its CAS makes the CAS lose, and that is
neither a success nor an error. Reporting `3 requested / 2 cancelled /
0 failed` leaves the reader concluding one link vanished.

``remaining`` is an INDEPENDENT observation of the state afterwards (the
recomputed live summary), not an arithmetic remainder — so it also catches
links created in parallel.

outage or a not-yet-widened credential must not stop a caller from

reporting it here is the ORIGINAL symptom of #417 — the agent proposing
every change instead of applying it, discovered a day later and after the
run was already paid for. This is what makes the gap visible immediately,
at the point where it was created.

Lifecycle of a `BalanceHold` document.

State machine (idempotent terminal transitions):

CourierKeysUpdateRequest.title: CourierKeysUpdateRequest
CourierKeysUpdateRequest.description:
One workspace's courier credential. Superadmin-only.

Field names carry weight and are not a style choice: `credential` and
`webhook_secret` are both in `_REDACTED_KEYS`, which is the only thing
keeping this body out of `ApiLog` — where it would sit for 90 days and be
re-served through `GET /api/v1/logs`. Renaming either one needs the new
name added there in the SAME commit.

`account` is the identifier half of the pair. It is stored inside the same
ciphertext as the secret, rather than beside it, because it is an e-mail
address: keeping it out of every response is cheaper than deciding later
which responses may carry it.

Omitting a field leaves it alone; that is what makes the channel
switchable off without re-sending the secret.

FeatureEnforcement.title: FeatureEnforcement
FeatureEnforcement.description:
WHOSE ``App.config`` the vertical's own server-side gate reads.

Not a nicety — it is the difference between a switch and a label.

``TENANT``: the gate resolves the App from ``current_user.app_id``, so
switching the feature off for a tenant blocks that tenant's users. Only
``ads`` does this today (``endpoints/ads.py::_tenant_config``).

``TOKEN_APP``: the gate reads ``current_app.config`` — the App of the BEARER
TOKEN, which for every dashboard user is the ``dashboard`` app rather than
their own tenant (``endpoints/deliveries.py``, ``endpoints/trading.py``).
Switching such a feature off for some *other* tenant removes its menu entry
(``GET /dashboard/modules`` IS per tenant) and does **not** block anything
server-side. The console says so rather than implying an enforcement it does
not have; making it true means changing where two live money verticals
resolve their config, which is a different epic.

FeatureSource.description:

The origin is the point of the whole screen: ``true`` does not tell an
operator whether the tenant was configured or is merely inheriting, and
"inheriting" is exactly the state every production tenant is in today —
none of the six has any of these keys written.

FeatureStateOut.description:
One (tenant, feature) cell.

``operable`` answers "can the provider-backed path run right now", NOT "is
the module dead". They differ for ``deliveries``, whose own-fleet mode needs
no provider at all (``delivery_service.py`` dispatches it without touching
the factory) while courier dispatch answers a typed 503 until one is
contracted. The UI copy says exactly that: the actions that need a provider
will fail.

FeatureTogglePatch.title: FeatureTogglePatch
FeatureTogglePatch.description:
Switch one feature for one tenant.

Three distinct operations, not two: ``true`` turns it on, ``false`` turns it
off **explicitly**, and ``null`` REMOVES the override so the tenant goes back
to inheriting. Omitting the field entirely is a fourth thing — "nothing to
change" — and answers 422, because a body that says nothing must not read as
a successful no-op the operator will believe.

The distinction is not free: it needs ``model_fields_set`` at the handler,
since ``enabled=None`` is both the default and a meaningful value. The
trading config patch next door already carries the same machinery for the
same reason.

an omitted field leaves the link as it is.

conversation: the person who wrote last. Letting the caller name them

domain to anyone" — the same capability, without the thread that justifies
it.

PluginCatalogResponseData.title: PluginCatalogResponseData
PluginCatalogResponseData.description:
Serves two purposes behind one endpoint and one cache-aside provider
(D-8/D-9), so a panel open costs exactly one call:

- ``results``: text search against the directory (WPG-10), populated
  only when ``q`` was given.
- ``abandoned``: slug → ISO timestamp of the directory's last release,
  for every slug in the site's CURRENT inventory whose directory lookup
  succeeded and crossed ``abandoned_after_months`` (WPG-09). A slug
  absent from this map is not necessarily maintained — the lookup may
  simply have failed open (D-9) — which is why the panel never renders
  "0 abandoned" from its absence, only "abandoned" from its presence.

PluginInventoryItemInput.title: PluginInventoryItemInput
PluginInventoryItemInput.description:
One plugin as the SITE reports it. Everything derived server-side
(``slug``, ``plugin_dir``, ``is_platform_plugin``) has no slot here —
a client-sent ``is_platform_plugin: true`` on "akismet" has nowhere to
land (T-7).

``file`` deliberately carries no ``pattern=`` here: the global
``RequestValidationError`` handler answers a Pydantic-level rejection
with ``{"detail": [...]}`` (measured, ``app/core/exception_handlers.py``),
not this surface's ``{success, data:{code}, msg}`` envelope. The shape is
validated in the SERVICE instead, so a malformed ``file`` (including path
traversal, T-6) raises ``PluginFileInvalidError`` and the client gets the
contracted ``plugin_file_invalid`` code — belt-and-suspenders with the
same pattern re-applied on the stored ``InstalledPlugin`` model.

PluginInventoryReplaceRequest.title: PluginInventoryReplaceRequest
PluginInventoryReplaceRequest.description:
``PUT /users/websites/{website_id}/plugins``. Replaces, never merges
(plan §5.2): whatever ``items`` does not name, the stored inventory no
longer has.

``total_reported`` is accepted for forward-compat with the wire shape
the plugin already sends, but it is NEVER trusted for the stored summary
(T-41) — the server always derives it from ``len(items)`` before
truncating to ``max_inventory_items``. A client cannot make the panel
undercount by lying in this field.

``source`` names which of D-7's four triggers is publishing (bootstrap,
a WordPress hook, the 1-minute poll, or a manual "Sync now" order) —
plan §6.2 stores it verbatim as ``last_sync_source`` and WPG-03/05
assert its exact value, so it has to travel on the wire even though the
plan's abbreviated example body omits it. Defaults to ``"poll"``, the
routine background case, so an old plugin build that never sends it
still gets a truthful source.

this model has not grown yet, gets a 202 for a site built without it, with
no 422 and no log line. That is how a theme chosen in the wizard could
reach this endpoint and never reach the store. Mirrors ``WordPressSpec``,
which has declared it since WPS-01.

next_attempt_at.title: Next Attempt At
next_attempt_at.description: When this site is next eligible for an unattended retry — and, while a retry is in flight, the LEASE that owns it (JVD D-11). One field for both because `run_auto_setup` rewrites the whole document up to 8 times: the sweep sets this forward BEFORE calling, so the function's own writes preserve the reservation instead of erasing it.

SearchConsoleSetup.title: SearchConsoleSetup
SearchConsoleSetup.description:
Progress of the unattended connect → publish → verify → sitemap chain.

Only sites 1Platform serves can run it: the chain publishes the ownership
tag itself, waits for the served HTML to carry it, proves ownership, and
submits the site's sitemap — all from the single action the user paid for.
Every step is recorded here because the work outlives the request that
started it, and the FREE detail read is the only thing the dashboard may
poll (the action endpoint charges).

next_attempt_at.description: Instant from which the site is a candidate again. A single indexable, sortable field, so the backoff after a failure is expressible as a filter — which `last_synced_at < now - cadence` is not, because it cannot see the failure count (SCS D-17).

reads with every field at its default, and the candidate query treats that as

Written ONLY through `WebsiteRepository.set_search_console_sync`, which
